prospects.name: JFrog

score_rationale.timing: CMO Genefa Murphy appointed Jan 5 2026 for a declared 'next growth phase'; FY2027 brand-budget planning is forming now.
score_rationale.capacity: FY2025 revenue $531.8M (+24%), $704.4M cash, $142.3M FCF, NDR 118%. A $3-5M/yr deal is immaterial.
score_rationale.brand_fit: No software-supply-chain-security brand is on the F1 grid (Confluent = data streaming). JFrog can OWN the category; Murphy's thesis 'trust, control, discipline at velocity' is a literal motorsport metaphor.
score_rationale.urgency: Rivals Sonatype/Snyk circle the same whitespace; first-mover locks the category for 3 years.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: a team's build/release pipeline is real software supply chain - JFrog tooling has a genuine in-garage engineering use, not just a logo.

prospects.headline_long: The CMO who built the Udemy-McLaren partnership now runs marketing at JFrog - a profitable, cash-rich public company - and the software-supply-chain-security slot on the F1 grid is still empty.
prospects.the_case: On 5 January 2026 JFrog appointed Genefa Murphy as Chief Marketing Officer for what it called its 'next growth phase' in AI-driven software supply chain management. Murphy is the decisive signal: at Udemy she personally architected the multi-series McLaren Racing partnership (F1, IndyCar, NEOM McLaren Formula E and Extreme E). She is a proven, repeat motorsport-sponsorship believer who now controls the brand budget of a company with $531.8M revenue (+24% YoY), $704.4M cash and $142.3M free cash flow. Her public thesis for JFrog - that 'as velocity increases there is an increasing need for trust, control and discipline across the software supply chain' - is a ready-made Formula 1 narrative. And the category is open: Confluent (data streaming) sits on Williams, but no software-supply-chain-security brand is anywhere on the grid.
prospects.why_now: Murphy is ~5 months into a mandate defined as a growth-phase reset - the moment a CMO sets the multi-year brand-investment agenda. She has done an F1/FE deal before, so the internal 'does motorsport work for B2B?' objection is pre-answered by her own track record. Move while the whitespace is empty, before a DevSecOps rival plants a flag.
prospects.why_team: McLaren is the warm path: Murphy knows the McLaren commercial organisation intimately from the Udemy partnership, and McLaren's technology-forward, precision-engineering identity mirrors JFrog's 'secure software, shipped fast' promise. Aston Martin is the fallback - premium CISO/CTO gravitas with an open DevSecOps slot.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. A modern F1 team ships thousands of software builds a season across simulation, strategy and car systems - that is a software supply chain. JFrog's platform offers a genuine technical-partner integration (artifact management, security scanning across the team's dev pipeline), not just branding. That earns authentic 'official software supply chain partner' storytelling McLaren can stand behind, plus enterprise hospitality where JFrog's CISO/CTO buyers already sit.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Software Supply Chain Partner tier on McLaren. MINIMUM THREE YEARS at an estimated $3-5M/yr, calibrated to JFrog's $531.8M revenue and $704M cash. Car/suit branding in the security category, garage and B2B hospitality, digital inventory, and a category-exclusivity clause so no DevSecOps rival follows.

decision_maker.title: Chief Marketing Officer, JFrog (appointed Jan 5 2026)
decision_maker.bio: Former Chief Marketing & Content Officer at Udemy, where she built the multi-series McLaren Racing partnership. Previously CMO of Five9, SVP & CMO of Micro Focus, and Global VP Corporate Marketing at HPE. A repeat motorsport-sponsorship dealmaker who now owns JFrog's brand budget.

prospects.opening_angle: "Genefa, you proved at Udemy that an F1 grid is a B2B channel, not a billboard. The software-supply-chain-security slot is still empty - JFrog can own the category McLaren's other tech partners can't. Can we book 25 minutes?"

risks.title: Budget cycle lag
risks.detail: A discretionary brand-sponsorship line may not be approved until FY2027.
risks.counter: Frame as a founder-level category land-grab; offer a short-form LOI to hold category exclusivity now.

risks.title: Founder alignment
risks.detail: Founder-CEO Shlomi Ben Haim is hands-on; a marquee spend needs his buy-in.
risks.counter: Position trust/security as JFrog's core message - a CEO narrative, not a marketing line item.

risks.title: B2B skepticism
risks.detail: Investors may question motorsport spend at a profit-inflecting company.
risks.counter: Murphy's Udemy-McLaren results are the proof case; lead with B2B pipeline outcomes, not impressions.

prospects.name: Cohesity

score_rationale.timing: Targeting a 2026 IPO - the brand-reckoning moment for a category leader; Veritas merger (Dec 2024) pushed ARR to ~$1.5B.
score_rationale.capacity: ARR ~$1.5B, 28% adjusted margin, Nvidia-backed, IPO valuation rivalling Rubrik's ~$17B. Easily funds title-adjacent spend.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Data security/resilience maps to F1's data-obsessed, zero-failure culture; no data-protection brand on the grid.
score_rationale.urgency: IPO window is a one-time elevation moment; Rubrik (public peer) raises category competitiveness.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A: an F1 team generates and must protect petabytes of telemetry and IP - a genuine data-resilience use case in the garage.

prospects.headline_long: Nvidia-backed Cohesity hit ~$1.5B ARR after absorbing Veritas and is steering toward a 2026 IPO at a valuation rivalling Rubrik's $17B - with no motorsport presence and an open data-security slot on the grid.
prospects.the_case: Cohesity is the rare combination our mandate prizes: a category leader at a brand-reckoning moment. Following its 2024 merger with Veritas' data-protection business, ARR surged to ~$1.5B at a 28% adjusted margin, and the Nvidia-backed company is eyeing a 2026 IPO with a valuation aimed at its public peer Rubrik (~$17B). It has never touched motorsport, so we would not be the 100th brand in the inbox - and the data-security/resilience category is unoccupied on the F1 grid.
prospects.why_now: An IPO is the single biggest brand-elevation moment a company gets. A multi-year F1 partnership signed around the listing converts a finance event into a global enterprise-brand statement and pre-builds the institutional credibility public investors reward.
prospects.why_team: Williams - the data-and-engineering revival story (Atlassian title, Confluent on data streaming) - is the natural canvas for a data-resilience brand, placing Cohesity beside complementary (not competing) data partners in front of enterprise IT buyers.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A. A Williams race weekend produces and must safeguard enormous volumes of telemetry, simulation output and design IP - exactly Cohesity's domain (backup, recovery, ransomware resilience). That supports an authentic technical-partner integration and 'we protect the data that wins races' storytelling, not a sticker.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Data Resilience Partner tier on Williams. MINIMUM THREE YEARS (ideally four to span the IPO and post-listing cycle), estimated $4-7M/yr. Garage/cockpit branding in the data-security category, hospitality at marquee rounds, digital rights for an enterprise-IT audience, category exclusivity.

decision_maker.bio: CEO Sanjay Poonen (ex-VMware) drives Cohesity's enterprise-brand and IPO narrative; confirm the current CMO and IR lead, who co-own brand-investment decisions during the listing window.

score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE B: back-office/treasury - Ramp serves the team's spend operation rather than the car.

prospects.headline_long: Ramp crossed $1B ARR in August 2025 and is in active talks for a $750M raise above $40B pre-money - a >25% step-change in six months - while opening a London office, with no spend-management brand anywhere on the grid.
prospects.the_case: Ramp's active $750M raise at above $40B pre-money is the BRAND RECKONING MOMENT - when a category-defining fintech transitions from growth story to institutional brand. With $100B+ annualized purchase volume, 50,000+ business customers and a freshly opened London office targeting EU/UK onboarding this summer, the commercial clock is running. No spend-management or AI-finance brand holds a position anywhere on the F1 grid; Brex has no motorsport deal. The slot that matches Ramp's Visa issuing relationship and EU/UK expansion arc is open at Visa Cash App Racing Bulls.
prospects.why_now: The $750M raise closes a short window, and the F1 London race in August 2026 is a live activation for Ramp's UK onboarding launch. Terms must be set before that calendar date locks.
prospects.why_team: Racing Bulls already carries Visa as title sponsor. Ramp's renewed multi-year Visa issuing agreement makes co-presence structural rather than conflicting - Ramp sits as the spend-management intelligence layer above the Visa rail. Cash App's younger demographic mirrors Ramp's CFO-suite and developer audience, and no competing spend-management brand is on the car.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE B. Ramp's payments rail and back-office stack map to Racing Bulls' commercial operation: paddock supplier settlements, sponsor-activation treasury flows, and a partner-onboarding funnel where venture-backed CFO-suite companies are the incoming audience. Ramp's Visa issuing partnership amplifies rather than displaces the title relationship. Surfaces: garage hospitality, pit-wall broadcast cuts, and digital founder-audience activation timed to the London race.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Spend Management Partner tier. FOUR YEARS to span the EU/UK build-out and capture two full FIA calendar rotations through London, Las Vegas and Austin. Estimated $6-9M/yr. Garage and cockpit logo rights, Visa co-activation rights, hospitality at London and Las Vegas, digital content rights for Ramp's CFO-audience channels.
